calls.prompt:
Company: SkyHop Airlines

US regional airline (~3,500 employees) flying short domestic routes from hubs in Denver and Salt Lake City. Fleet is 60 Embraer E175 jets and 25 Airbus A320-family jets (A319 and A320). Sells tickets online and at airports, charges bag fees, and runs its own maintenance hangar. Does not fly Boeing aircraft, Airbus A220/A350, or helicopters; no cargo-only flights, no international routes.

Rules that APPLY:
- FAA airworthiness directives for Embraer E175 (ERJ 170 family) or Airbus A319/A320, and their engines
- FAA rules for airline operations, pilots, crew rest and drug/alcohol testing
- DOT consumer rules for airline passengers (refunds, fees, accessibility)
- Airspace or airport rules at Denver or Salt Lake City, and airport fees charged to passengers
- TSA security rules for airlines

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Airworthiness directives for aircraft models we do not fly (Boeing, A220, A350, business jets, small planes, helicopters)
- Airspace changes at airports we do not serve
- Commercial space launches, drones, air-traffic-control equipment
- Banking, food, pharmacy, energy

Affected areas and owners:
- maintenance: Airworthiness directives, inspections, parts for our fleet → Carlos Mendez (Director of Maintenance)
- flight-ops: Flight operations, pilots and crew rules, airspace at our hubs → Jenna Holt (Flight Operations)
- customers: Passenger rights, refunds, fees, accessibility (DOT) → Omar Haddad (Customer Policy)
- safety-security: Drug/alcohol testing, TSA security, safety programs → Grace Liu (Safety & Security)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-06 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if it is a rule or proposed rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-11-06, or a final rule that took effect within the 30 days before 2026-11-06; otherwise High for final rules, Medium for proposed rules and for notices with a deadline, Low for anything else), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.

I found two documents that affect SkyHop. Both are proposed rules published in the window, and both are Critical. My searches had a limit, so I could not do a full sweep of every document in the window (see the end).

## 1. Airbus A319/A320 overhead stowage bin AD (proposed rule)
- **Document number:** 2026-22587
- **Title:** Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/05/2026-22587/airworthiness-directives-airbus-sas-airplanes
- **Published:** 2026-11-05
- **Key deadline:** Comments are due to the FAA by December 21, 2026.
- **Tier:** Critical. It is a proposed rule, and the deadline is 45 days after 2026-11-06.
- **Owner area:** maintenance (Carlos Mendez)
- **Reason:** The proposed AD covers A319 and A320 models. It was prompted by damage to the YZ-axis attachment points on airplanes with certain overhead stowage compartment bins.
- **Action:** The AD would require a one-time inspection of the affected bins, corrective action depending on findings, and a ban on installing affected parts. Check which A319/A320 tails have the ARIES overhead bins. Estimate the inspection workload and decide by December 21 whether to file comments.

## 2. Passenger Facility Charge regulations (proposed rule)
- **Document number:** 2026-22450
- **Title:** Update and Clarification of the Passenger Facility Charge Regulations
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-22450. I did not retrieve the full-slug page, so this is the short link for the document number.
- **Published:** 2026-11-04
- **Key deadline:** Comments are due January 4, 2027.
- **Tier:** Critical. It is a proposed rule, and the deadline is 59 days after 2026-11-06.
- **Owner area:** customers (Omar Haddad)
- **Reason:** It is an FAA proposed rule (12 pages) on Passenger Facility Charge regulations. PFCs are airport fees that appear on SkyHop tickets at Denver and Salt Lake City. I judged relevance from the title and the FAA's listing, and did not read the full text.
- **Action:** Review the proposed PFC changes for effects on how SkyHop collects, displays and remits PFCs at DEN and SLC. Decide whether to comment by January 4, 2027.

## Reviewed and excluded
- **2026-22382 (Embraer, 2026-11-03):** This proposed AD applies to Embraer ERJ 190-100 and -200 models. The E175 is in the ERJ 170 family, so it does not apply. Carlos Mendez's team may want to confirm this when they check the fleet.
- **2026-22665 (Airbus A350, 2026-11-06):** It applies only to A350-941 and -1041 airplanes, which SkyHop does not fly.

## Coverage gaps
My searches did not surface any of the following in the 11/02–11/06 window:
- E175 ADs
- engine ADs for the CF34 or CFM56-5B
- crew-rest or drug-and-alcohol rules
- TSA aircraft-operator rules
- Denver or Salt Lake City airspace actions

I did not confirm that none exist. A direct federalregister.gov search of those dates by agency and topic would close the gap.
